title: I Used the Table-Tennis Robot Hours on the Captain Who Palmed My Balls

parts.text: I stepped into table four at 7:08 p.m. and captain Rhea was already using my numbered balls. The board said: FORTY MINUTES. ROBOT BALLS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-seven, league lead, holding a clipboard that listed our drill. Rhea shrugged. "Captains keep the robot." I photographed the board, the booking, and her hopper on my robot. Then I asked for the robot hours. At 7:16 the rec desk pinged why Rhea's hopper sat on our robot. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The rec desk can see Rhea's hopper on table four during our drill.

social.video_title: She palmed my numbered robot balls — Part 1/2
social.description: Table tennis, a captain on my robot, a forty-minute clock she posted. I logged the hopper. Would you have asked for the robot hours?

parts.text: Rhea called it multiball until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the hopper still. The balls went back to my numbered tub. Rhea ran a slot of their own and told the next captain atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CAPTAINS DO NOT KEEP THE ROBOT. I keep our drill on a labeled card. Rhea brown-bags her hoppers. The table finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.
